Looking back on this almost 20 years later and my biggest takeaway is how insecure this movie is. Dark Knight is CONSTANTLY SCREAMING its themes at you in the most dramatic, self indulgent way possible. You’ll have the Joker literally look at the screen and state “I’m an agent of chaos” while Gordon and Batman wax poetically on whether people are naturally good or evil. Worst of all, the movie will go out of its way to tell the viewer that some people are simply irredeemable and need to be put down. Contrast that to how the Spider-Man movies will try to tackle the heavy subject of villain redemption. Sure the execution is childish but at least it tries!   I came away with the theory that Nolan thought that superhero movies were not good enough to stand on their own so he had to water this down into the most grounded, serious, “adult” version of the Batman possible. The problem isn’t that The Dark Knight has nothing to say. It’s that it has so much confidence in how profound those things are that it rarely bothers to dramatize them. The movie is a long, slow, plodding mess that does not get the buy in necessary to take it self so seriously. Two hours and thirty minutes and no one gets developed. Gordon is always right and never pushed to grow, Harvey’s turn felt superficial and rudimentary, Rachel was literally in the movie to die. Worst of all, the Joker. We get so much time to develop and build on them relationship between him and Batman; how they’re mirrors of each other, how their philosophies are contradictory, how they mess with each other’s head. Instead we get Joker stating funny quips and theorize on le society. And I’m sorry but this movie and this performance is no where near good enough to justify the worship the Joker and this movie at large gets.

I completely understand why people call this one of the greatest superhero films ever made. I just don’t love it as much as everyone else seems to. Heath Ledger is obviously incredible. Every scene with the Joker has this horrible sense that anything could happen, and he completely owns the film. The interrogation scene alone deserves all the praise it gets. The problem for me is that outside of the Joker, I find parts of it a bit cold. Christian Bale’s Batman works, but Bruce Wayne never connects with me as much as other versions of the character, and Harvey Dent’s arc feels slightly rushed considering how important he becomes by the end. It’s brilliantly made, looks great and has some genuinely iconic moments, but I admire it more than I actually enjoy watching it.

Para mí, The Dark Knight es la mejor película de la trilogía. Lo que más me gustó fue la forma en que se desarrolla el personaje de The Joker y cómo se opone ante Batman para intentar destruir Gotham. La historia es más compleja y madura que la de la primera película, y se nota que Nolan elevó el nivel en todos los aspectos. La actuación de Heath Ledger como Joker me pareció excelente. Consigue transmitir perfectamente la locura y el caos del personaje, convirtiéndolo en uno de los villanos más memorables del cine. Aunque hay momentos en los que la película puede sentirse un poco lenta o pesada, especialmente por su duración, sigue siendo una experiencia que vale la pena. Al terminarla me dejó una muy buena sensación y entendí por qué tanta gente la considera una de las mejores películas de superhéroes de todos los tiempos. Algo que hace especial a esta película es la forma en que Christopher Nolan utilizó cámaras IMAX para muchas de las escenas más importantes. Esto permitió mostrar Gotham, las persecuciones y las secuencias de acción con una escala impresionante que todavía hoy se siente espectacular. Además, Nolan intentó evitar el uso excesivo de CGI, prefiriendo efectos prácticos siempre que fuera posible. Gracias a esto, muchas escenas conservan una sensación de realismo que las hace envejecer mejor que otras películas de superhéroes de la misma época. Esa combinación entre IMAX, efectos prácticos y una dirección muy cuidada es una de las razones por las que la trilogía sigue siendo tan recordada.

Получше первого фильма, но всё так же много несуразностей, благоглупостей. Сюжет как сюжет, комиксовый, но смотреть скучно. Почему? Игра актёров средненькая, запомнились разве Аарон Экхарт (прокурор Дент, «двуликий») хорошей игрой и Мэгги Джиленхолл нулевой игрой (а в фильме они - пара, то есть сыграли «на контрасте»). Единственный актёр-монстр фильма - Хит Леджер, и теперь Джокер может быть только таким, а мир не может быть прежним. Без Леджера фильм остался бы лишь раскрашенным картонным комиксом, где много взрывается, мчится и летает, но это неинтересно. Рассудочный гений Нолана делает красивую картинку, но на этом и всё. Как ни странно, пришла мысль, что Нолан не знает, что такое хорошая актёрская игра, и потому не требует её от актёров. Сериал «Готам» перекрывает «Рыцаря» по всем статьям.

Obviously a step up from the previous one, but still: Most of the problems transfer (although way less severe) to this movie. The tone is constantly dangling between ridiculous extravaganza and grounded seriousness, which again results in a strange Grey soup of misplaced one liners followed by almost laughably schmaltzy speeches delivered by the (mostly) undercooked cast. I never really cared for this Joker, and I find it ridiculous that people talk about him like he's the greatest antagonist of all time. Heath Ledger is good, still prefer Nicholsons soap opera comic gangsterboss. Bale feels at times like he's parodying himself. The best part is easily the truck chase under the bridge, and its pretty much the only part that I think about when I think about this film.

3/5 I’m retroactively doing this review as a point. This movie is only remembered for Heath Ledger dying. If he didn’t die, then no one would’ve really cared. Fine job, best performance? Ehhh. He had one good line. Rachel was a shell of what she was in BB. She essentially was a damsel in distress the whole time. Harvey was a joke and not worth the effort Nolan put into him. This was a pretentious dark movie with a Batman paint job on it. Batman Begins was the best in the trilogy. And there are better CBMs out there.
